axes.model_access:
Same as the CLI form: Anthropic's own Claude family.

**v2.1.284 (2026-09-28) added Claude Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`),
1M context.** (API pricing on the official pricing page; not stored by this site.)

This model update comes from the CHANGELOG — the only subject in this collection whose default-model spec was verified from a changelog.
axes.runtime:
**One process, three usages** (README original wording):

"Use it in your terminal, **IDE**, or tag @claude on Github."

That is: terminal, IDE, and triggering via an `@claude` mention on GitHub.
**These three are different entry points of the same tool, not three implementations** —
unlike [Cline's three forms](../../coding/products/cline.md) (three independent forms).
axes.local_files:
**The permission model is strongly tied to the working directory** (official security page, "Working directory boundary"):
in Manual mode, file tools ask before reading/writing outside the launch directory and its subdirectories.

To read a directory without asking, add it as an additional directory
(`--add-dir` / `/add-dir` / `additionalDirectories`).

**Reads can be allowed or denied precisely by path**:

- the official `permissions.deny` examples in settings are `"Read(./.env)"`, `"Read(./.env.*)"`
- the `permissions.allow` example is `"Bash(npm run test *)"`

**Bash additionally has an OS-level sandbox** (official sandboxing page, off by default):

with `sandbox.enabled`, writes default to the working directory + temp directory + added directories,
reads default to the whole machine (including credential files like `~/.ssh`, tightenable via `denyRead`).

1M context. **These three mechanisms are read from the same settings files by the VS Code / JetBrains extensions and the terminal**
(official settings page), so the IDE form applies the same boundaries.
axes.background:
**The IDE extension itself is a local process** — quit and it stops (local sessions can be driven remotely from a phone/browser via Remote Control, but execution still happens on your machine).

**But the same tool provides a "real background"**: cloud sessions (`claude --cloud` / claude.ai/code)
run on Anthropic-managed cloud infrastructure.

**Official wording**: "The session keeps running after you close your laptop"

They can be started and viewed from browser, phone, desktop or terminal; there is also GitHub Actions
(`@claude`, `prompt` automations, `schedule` timed runs) plus Routines scheduled/triggered runs — each execution counts as one cloud session.

**Cloud sessions being available does not mean local IDE sessions can run in the background** — the execution environments differ.
axes.tools:
**Built-in tools + MCP + extension mechanisms are all there.**

Built-in file and web tools (Read / Edit / Write / WebFetch / WebSearch),
Bash, LSP etc. (official tools-reference).

**MCP support is complete** (official mcp page):

transports include **HTTP / SSE / stdio / WebSocket**.
Install scopes come in three levels: local / project (`.mcp.json`) / user,
configured with `claude mcp add`, supporting `mcpServers` JSON import and OAuth auth.

v2.1.284 also added `/mcp reconnect all` and fixed the race where MCP tools reported
"No such tool available" on session resume (**now waits up to 10 seconds**).

**Extension mechanisms**:

- Hooks (ConfigChange / PreToolUse etc.)
- Subagents (each with its own context and optional persistent memory)
- Plugins
- Skills
- `.claude/rules/` rules

The three entry points (terminal / IDE / GitHub) share the same set.
axes.context:
**Cross-session memory has an explicit hierarchy** (official memory page):

CLAUDE.md comes in four levels — managed policy / user (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) /
project (`./CLAUDE.md` or `./.claude/CLAUDE.md`) / local
(`CLAUDE.local.md`) — loaded broad-to-narrow and concatenated.

CLAUDE.md files in subdirectories are loaded on demand, when files in that directory are read.

There is also **auto memory** (notes Claude writes itself, first 200 lines / 25KB loaded per session)
and `.claude/rules/` (file types limitable via `paths:`).

**Compaction runs automatically**: near the limit it auto-`/compact`,
and the official context-window page gives the retention rules for each mechanism after compaction
(the project-root CLAUDE.md and auto memory are re-injected from disk).

v2.1.284 fixed the persistent "still too long after compacting" error (it compacts once more).

Models supporting 1M context have a separate `[1m]` variant.

**The three entry points read the same CLAUDE.md set and use the same compaction strategy, so IDE and CLI are consistent.**
axes.permissions:
**The finest permission design in this category**, shared across forms:

settings use `allow` / `ask` / `deny` rule classes keyed by tool and content,
with official examples `"allow": ["Bash(npm run lint)"]`, `"deny": ["Read(./.env)"]`.

Rules come from four levels of settings files (user / project / project-local / managed),
with managed settings taking highest precedence.

Permission modes include:

- auto (reviewed by a classifier model)
- manual (read-only start, ask one by one)
- acceptEdits
- plan
- bypassPermissions
- dontAsk

It also offers the third state "allow this once but keep asking".

Managed policies support `availableModels` and `enforceAvailableModels`,
warning at startup on mismatch; `/usage` shows concrete dollar amounts rather than percentages.

**Bash additionally has an OS-level sandbox** (official sandboxing page, off by default):

once enabled, filesystem and network are doubly isolated (no network egress by default; a local proxy with a domain allowlist).
Supported on macOS / Linux / WSL2; not supported on native Windows.
Credential storage: macOS uses Keychain, Linux uses a 0600 file.

**The VS Code and JetBrains extensions read the same settings files** (official settings page),
so the permission mechanisms above apply to the IDE form.
axes.fit:
People already using an IDE who want Claude without switching tools.
People who need the same tool across terminal, IDE and GitHub.
People who value controllable permissions and the MCP ecosystem.

sections.形态澄清（与 Cline 的关键区别）:
README original wording:

```
Use it in your terminal, IDE, or tag @claude on Github.
```

**Note the wording**: it says "use it in",
**not "install"**.

### The essential difference from Cline's three forms

| | Claude Code | Cline |
|---|---|---|
| Three usages | terminal / IDE / GitHub | CLI / Desktop / VS Code extension |
| Implementation | **the same process** | **three independent forms** |
| Release lines | one (v2.1.x) | two (v4.x + desktop-v0.0.x) |
| Permission mechanics | shared across forms | each form independent |

**This difference matters to users**:
Claude Code's permissions and sessions are consistent across the three entry points,
while Cline's three forms may evolve separately.
sections.权限设计（本分区最细，且多态共用）:
This is the most valuable part of Claude Code, **and because it is shared across forms, understanding it once applies everywhere**:

### ① Asks per path + a third-state option

v2.1.284 added:

```
Added a "Yes, but ask again next time" answer to auto mode's prompt
before a read outside the working directories
```

Most tools' approvals have only two states — allow / deny.
Here there is a third state: **allow this once, but keep asking**.

### ② Managed policies control usable models

In enterprise scenarios `availableModels` controls usable models,
`enforceAvailableModels` decides whether it is enforced,
and **mismatches warn at startup** — no silent degradation.

### ③ Quota shows concrete amounts

CHANGELOG original text (excerpt; amount examples not quoted per D9 policy):

```
Added dollar amounts to the Claude apps gateway spend limit in /usage
and the status line
```

`/usage` and the status line show amounts rather than abstract percentages.
sections.上下文压缩的边界处理:
```
Fixed "Prompt is too long" errors that persisted after compacting:
now compacts once more, keeping less of the recent conversation
```

**After compaction a request may still be too long**; then it compacts once more and keeps less of the recent conversation.
This is honest boundary handling — not pretending one compaction solves everything.
sections.MCP 支持与一个值得注意的修复:
Two v2.1.284 changes:

| Type | Content |
|---|---|
| added | `/mcp reconnect all` |
| fixed | on session resume MCP tools reported "No such tool available" (the server was still connecting); it now **waits up to 10 seconds** |

**The second one reveals a real scenario**: a race exists between session resume and MCP connection.
Only heavy usage would surface this class of problem.

start a session in the IDE, switch to the terminal to continue, and check whether permission state and context are fully preserved.
Because the official claims the forms are shared, this claim must be verified.
